Dulse and Oatcakes

Served at: Imbolc Day Celebration

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 15 min

Dulse is a type of edible red seaweed traditionally harvested along the coasts of Ireland and Scotland. It is often enjoyed during Imbolc, a Celtic festival marking the beginning of spring, symbolizing renewal and the gathering of natural foods. This simple recipe pairs dulse with homemade oatcakes, a traditional accompaniment during Imbolc celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup rolled oats (90 g)
  • 1/4 cup whole wheat flour (30 g)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon baking powder
  • 3 tablespoons melted butter (45 ml)
  • 1/3 cup water (80 ml), plus more if needed
  • 1/2 cup dried dulse flakes (about 10 g)
  • Butter or cream cheese for serving

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. In a bowl, combine rolled oats, whole wheat flour, salt, and baking powder.
  3. Add melted butter and water to the dry ingredients and mix until a dough forms. Add a little more water if the dough is too dry.
  4. Roll the dough out on a floured surface to about 1/4 inch (0.6 cm) thickness.
  5. Cut the dough into rounds or squares and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
  6. Bake in the oven for 12-15 minutes until golden and crisp.
  7. While oatcakes bake, soak dried dulse flakes in warm water for 5 minutes to rehydrate, then drain.
  8. Serve oatcakes warm with softened butter or cream cheese topped with rehydrated dulse flakes.

Tips

  • Use fresh dulse if available for a more vibrant flavor.
  • Oatcakes can be stored in an airtight container for up to a week.
  • For a vegan option, substitute butter with olive oil or coconut oil.
